label: input-phase o/a/k/p/u token (context-gated)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively in the original (input) phase at t>=1 (99.8% of mass; never at t=0, the delimiter, or in the copy phase), when the current input token is one of o, a, k, p (and to a lesser degree u, f, n, v, d). Strongly prefers first occurrences of the token (in_first 93% of mass). These tokens are necessary but far from sufficient: only ~11-13% of such steps are active, and the gating depends on the preceding context in a way no simple predicate captures. Sequences starting with y (4.5x lift) and previous input i or n (5.8x, 3.7x) raise firing rate and magnitude; the top activations are o/a/p/n right after an i in sequences beginning with y. Rates are highest at t=1..4 and fall off later in long sequences. Predicate covers ~85% of activation mass but has low precision (~11%), so the explanation is incomplete.
